html:
A town in Rakhine State, western Myanmar, that was the capital of the kingdom of Arakan from 1430 until 1785. In its prime it was a rich trading port filled with stone temples.

The kingdom was founded by King Min Saw Mon, who had spent years in exile at the court of the Bengal Sultanate and came back with its help. For a time Arakan's kings used Muslim titles beside Buddhist ones and minted coins in Persian script. The city lay inland on tidal creeks, easy to defend, and traded rice, slaves and goods with Bengal, the Portuguese, the Dutch East India Company and others.

In the 16th and 17th centuries Arakan was a sea power. With Portuguese adventurers it raided the Bengal coast for captives. The Mughal prince Shah Shuja fled here in 1660 and was killed. The great temples, such as the Shitthaung and Koe-thaung, were built of stone like fortresses. In 1785 the Konbaung kings of Burma conquered Arakan and carried off its holiest image, the Mahamuni Buddha. The city declined after that.
sum: A town in Rakhine State, western Myanmar, that was the capital of the kingdom of Arakan from 1430 until 1785. In its prime it was a rich trading port filled with stone temples.
